chunks: “If a junub enters the well, seven buckets are drawn from it.”

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If blood falls into it and it is much, ten buckets are drawn from it; and if it is little, five buckets are drawn from it. This is taken from the report which follows.

— (705) 36 — Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed us of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:

I wrote to a man asking him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a well in the house used for wudu (ablution), into which drops of urine or blood drip, or something from excrement such as a pellet or the like falls into it: what purifies it so that wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) from it becomes permissible? So he عليه السلام wrote in my letter, in his own hand: “Buckets are to be drawn from it.”

The aspect of inference from this report is that he said: “Buckets are to be drawn from it,” and the highest number added to this plural is ten; therefore it is necessary that we adopt it and hold to it, since there is no proof for anything less than that.
Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If a snake falls into it and dies, three buckets are drawn from it; and likewise if a gecko falls into it.

key_terms.الْبِئْرَ: the well whose water is being discussed
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution) performed with the well water
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood falling into the well as an impurity
key_terms.عَذِرَةٍ: filth or excrement contaminating the well
key_terms.نُزِحَ: water is drawn out from the well
key_terms.وَزَغَةٌ: a gecko falling into the well

ai.seo_question: How many buckets must be drawn from a well if impurity such as blood, urine, or a dead animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings on purifying well water when it is contaminated by ritual impurity or filth, specifying numbers of buckets to be drawn in different cases. It also records a report from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام and presents the juristic reasoning used by al-Shaykh in deriving the quantity required for purification.
